title: ALDI Recalls Two Priano Tortelloni Pastas Over Botulism Risk in Four States
excerpt: ALDI has recalled two Priano protein tortelloni pastas because they may not have been kept at the right temperature, creating a possible risk of botulism, a pot
content:
ALDI has recalled two Priano protein tortelloni pastas because they may not have been kept at the right temperature, creating a possible risk of botulism, a potentially life-threatening illness. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration published the recall notice Nov. 17, 2026.

The recalled products are Priano Protein Carbonara Tortelloni and Priano Protein Herb & Cheese Tortelloni, sold in 9-ounce plastic units, lot T9101926, with a best-if-used-by date of Dec. 18, 2026.

The pastas were sold at select ALDI stores in Alabama, Georgia, North Carolina and South Carolina, in stores and online. They were not sold in Texas, so this is a national consumer alert for Laredo readers who may have bought them while traveling or had them shipped.

The problem: the products may not have been stored, distributed or sold at appropriate temperatures, which can allow the growth of pathogens including Clostridium botulinum, the bacterium that causes botulism. The FDA warns consumers not to eat the recalled pastas even if they look and smell fine.

No illnesses had been reported as of Nov. 17, according to the recall notice.

Consumers who have the recalled tortelloni should throw it away or return it to the store. ALDI's consumer line is 844-484-0332.

Botulism is rare but serious. The FDA notice is a precaution tied to temperature control, not a finding that the product itself was contaminated at the factory — and no illnesses have been linked to these lots so far.
